- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the low-end to reflect market resilience.  
- Forecast errors often occur in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon — adjust early values downward if sentiment is weak or upward if sentiment is strong.  
- After a significant price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecasted decline by 2–5% to allow for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (0.0–0.2), forecast should be closer to historical mean of last 7–10 days, not extrapolated from recent extremes.  
- Overshoots in the 20–30 day horizon are common when sentiment is rising — cap forecast at 1.5x recent high if sentiment > 0.5.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 2–3% to capture momentum.
